stem: A 47-year-old day laborer with several years of stone-cutting and construction work presents with about ten weeks of cough and progressive breathlessness, previously diagnosed with silicosis two years ago after a workplace health screening. He assumed his current symptoms were simply his silicosis worsening, as it often does gradually. He has lost some weight recently, which his family attributes to reduced appetite from his breathing difficulty. No prior TB treatment, no known contact with drug-resistant TB, no HIV risk factors. Sputum smear negative, Xpert MTB/RIF positive, rifampicin not detected. Chest imaging shows nodular silicotic changes bilaterally without a discrete new cavity. Exam: reduced breath sounds bilaterally, scattered crackles, mild digital clubbing.

patient.social_history: Long history of occupational silica exposure; previously diagnosed silicosis followed intermittently
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough, progressive breathlessness, weight loss, initially attributed to known silicosis
patient.exam_findings: Reduced breath sounds bilaterally, scattered crackles, mild digital clubbing, bilateral nodular silicotic changes without a discrete new cavity on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: Progression of known silicosis proposed as sufficient explanation for the breathlessness and weight loss without considering a superimposed process
Reduced appetite attributed entirely to baseline breathing difficulty rather than a new systemic illness
ntep_correct_actions: Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Administer first-line anti-TB therapy on a daily dosing schedule throughout both the intensive and continuation phases; do not offer an intermittent (thrice- or twice-weekly) dosing option.
Dose first-line anti-TB drugs using a fixed-dose-combination tablet count assigned by the patient's weight band, not a per-kilogram calculation performed at the point of care.
who_correct_actions: Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Administer first-line anti-TB therapy on a daily dosing schedule throughout both the intensive and continuation phases; do not offer an intermittent (thrice- or twice-weekly) dosing option.
Dose first-line anti-TB drugs using a fixed-dose-combination tablet count assigned by the patient's weight band, not a per-kilogram calculation performed at the point of care.
us_correct_actions: Send both liquid and solid mycobacterial culture on the initial specimen regardless of the molecular test result, since culture is considered the gold-standard microbiologic test.

Continuation-phase dosing may be switched to thrice-weekly (or twice-weekly if directly observed therapy is difficult), since this patient is HIV-negative and at low relapse risk (non-cavitary, smear-negative disease).
Calculate this patient's anti-TB drug doses individually in mg/kg based on current body weight, rather than assigning a fixed tablet count by weight band.
critical_error_conditions: Ruling out TB based on the negative smear alone without acting on the positive molecular result
Placing this patient on an intermittent dosing schedule from the start of the intensive phase, which is never appropriate regardless of relapse risk
expected_divergence_points: Whether mycobacterial culture is ordered as a mandatory parallel test or reserved for the resistance cascade
Whether daily dosing is used throughout treatment or intermittent dosing is offered for a low-relapse-risk patient
Whether drug dosing is assigned via a weight-band FDC tablet count or calculated individually in mg/kg
